findings.diagnosis: The prompt treats head–complement splits too crudely: it does not consistently recognize when a predicate, required complement, or scope-bearing operator (objects, prepositional complements, negation, complement clauses) is cohesion-critical, so cuts that strand these elements are ranked as if harmless and produce misleading or contradictory fragments.
findings.evidence: en_us_1507,en_us_1280,en_us_154,en_us_1342,en_us_1600,en_us_1497,en_us_1428,en_us_1285 — all contain policy cuts that separate predicates or required complements (prepositions/objects, negation scopes, complement clauses) producing low H_set or high contra while the target reunites them.

edit.target: Watch for incomplete subordinate or conditional fragments whose complement appears later;
edit.text: Penalize cuts that leave a predicate or an obligatory complement/scope-bearing element (verb objects, prepositional complements, complement clauses, negation scope) on the other side when the pre-cut span alone would assert or plausibly imply a claim; allow cuts inside optional modifiers or long NPs when they do not create a standalone misleading assertion.
